body:
# Each value can flow into the next command.
[1 2 3] | math sum

# A bare value is already a complete command.
print 42

# Sum a list, then take the absolute value.
[1 2 3] | math sum | math abs

# Describe a result after you compute it.
[1 2 3] | math sum | describe

# Turn a sum into text and count its characters.
[1 2 3 4] | math sum | into string | str length

# Keep the numbers that pass a test.
[1 2 3] | where {|n| $n > 1} | math sum

# Chain four steps from a list to a length.
[1 2 3 4] | math sum | into string | str length | math abs

# A pipe sends one command's output into the next.
[1 2 3] | math sum

# Parentheses run a pipeline where a value is expected.
1 + (2 | math abs)

# Two pipes can compute and then format.
[8 1] | math max | into string

# skip drops a prefix before length counts.
[1 2 3 4] | skip 1 | length

# Three pipes reduce, convert, and measure.
[5 5] | math sum | into string | str length

# A closure in the middle is still a pipeline.
[1 2 3] | each {|n| $n + 1} | math sum

# Four pipes is a small program.
[1 2 3 4] | math sum | into string | str length | math abs

# describe reports the type of a value.
42 | describe

# A record is a set of named fields.
{name: "nu"} | describe

# into string changes a number into text.
7 | into string | str length

# into int reads digits from text.
"12" | into int | math abs

# Convert, measure, and convert back.
99 | into string | str length | into string

# Check the type of each list item.
[1 "a"] | each {|n| $n | describe} | length

# Walk a number through four conversions.
12 | into string | str length | into string | str length

# str uppercase changes letters to capitals.
"nushell" | str uppercase

# str length counts characters.
"tips" | str length

# Split text, then count the pieces.
"a-b-c" | split row "-" | length

# Replace a word, then measure the text.
"red fish" | str replace "red" "blue" | str length

# Trim, split, and count the words.
" a b " | str trim | split row " " | length

# Build a line from each word.
["do" "learn"] | each {|w| $"go ($w)"} | str join " "

# Four string steps from trim to a count.
" a-b " | str trim | split row "-" | length | math abs

# length counts the items in a list.
[1 2 3] | length

# first returns the item at the front.
[4 5 6] | first

# append adds an item, then sum the list.
[1 2] | append 3 | math sum

# skip drops a prefix, then length counts.
[1 2 3 4] | skip 1 | length

# reverse, take, and sum a short list.
[1 2 3 4] | reverse | take 2 | math sum

# Add one to each item, then sum.
[1 2 3] | each {|n| $n + 1} | math sum

# Sort, skip, take, and sum.
[3 1 4 2] | sort | skip 1 | take 2 | math sum

# get reads one field from a record.
{name: "nu"} | get name

# columns lists the field names.
{a: 1, b: 2} | columns

# insert adds a field you can read back.
{a: 1} | insert b 2 | get b

# upsert writes a field even when it exists.
{a: 1} | upsert a 5 | get a

# Merge two records and count the fields.
{a: 1} | merge {b: 2} | columns | length

# Visit each field value.
{a: 1, b: 2} | items {|k, v| $v} | math sum

# Insert a field, then measure its text.
{a: 1} | insert b 22 | get b | into string | str length

# get pulls one column from a table.
[{a: 1} {a: 2}] | get a

# length counts the rows of a table.
[{a: 1} {a: 2}] | length

# Sum one column of a table.
[{a: 1} {a: 4}] | get a | math sum

# select keeps the columns you name.
[{a: 1, b: 2}] | select a | get a

# Reject a column, then count what remains.
[{a: 1, b: 2}] | reject b | columns | length

# Update a cell with a small closure.
[{a: 1}] | update a {|row| $row.a + 1} | get a

# Sum a column and report its width.
[{n: 3} {n: 4}] | get n | math sum | into string | str length

# A cell path walks nested fields.
{user: {name: "nu"}} | get user.name

# get can read a list by index.
[10 20 30] | get 1

# Step through nested fields one by one.
{user: {name: "nu"}} | get user | get name

# Read a nested record from a one-row table.
[{user: {name: "nu"}}] | get user | get name

# A path, a row, and a length.
[{user: {name: "ada"}}] | get user.name | first | str length

# Choose rows, then read a field.
[{n: 1} {n: 3}] | where {|row| $row.n > 1} | get n

# Drill into a column and measure the text.
[{user: {name: "ada"}}] | get user.name | first | str length | math abs

# let names a value for later lines.
let x = 3
$x

# Use a stored list in one pipe.
let n = [1 2 3]
$n | math sum

# Add a stored number, then take abs.
let n = 4
($n + 1) | math abs | into string

# mut lets a later line change the value.
mut n = 1
$n = 2
$n | math abs | into string

# Three steps from a stored list.
let n = [1 2 3 4]
$n | math sum | into string | str length

# A closure can read an outer variable.
let bonus = 2
[1 2] | each {|n| $n + $bonus} | math sum

# Store a list, then run four pipes.
let n = [1 2 3 4]
$n | math sum | into string | str length | math abs

# + adds two numbers.
2 + 3

# == compares two values.
2 == 2

# Parentheses group two abs calls.
(3 | math abs | math abs)

# Add two piped absolute values.
(1 | math abs) + (2 | math abs)

# Three math steps inside parentheses.
(8 | math abs | into string | str length)

# Compare each number with a closure.
[1 2 3] | where {|n| $n > 2} | length

# Four arithmetic stages on a list.
[2 3 4] | math sum | math abs | into string | str length

# if chooses one branch.
if 1 < 2 { "yes" } else { "no" }

# match picks a branch by value.
match 2 { 2 => "two" }

# A pipe can feed the condition.
if ([1 2 3] | math sum | math abs) > 0 { "ok" }

# for walks a list and a later line sums it.
mut total = 0
for n in [1 2] { $total = $total + $n }
$total | math abs | into string

# Three pipes decide the branch.
if ([1 2 3 4] | math sum | into string | str length) > 0 { "ok" }

# each can branch on every item.
[1 2 3] | each {|n| if $n > 1 { $n } else { 0 }} | math sum

# first keeps the opening item.
[9 8 7] | first

# last 1 keeps the final item.
[9 8 7] | last 1

# take and skip window a list.
[1 2 3 4] | skip 1 | take 2

# uniq drops repeated items.
[1 1 2 2] | uniq | length

# where can test a column without a closure.
[{n: 1} {n: 2} {n: 3}] | where n > 1 | length | math abs

# where with a closure keeps the matches.
[1 2 3 4] | where {|n| $n > 2} | math sum

# skip, take, sum, and abs.
[1 2 3 4] | skip 1 | take 2 | math sum | math abs

# do runs a block and returns its value.
do { "hello" }

# A block can hold one expression.
do { 1 + 2 }

# Pipe the block result twice.
do { [1 2 3] } | math sum | math abs

# A block can produce the list you sum.
do { [1 2 3] } | math sum | into string

# Three pipes after a do block.
do { [1 2 3 4] } | math sum | into string | str length

# each is an anonymous command.
[1 2 3] | each {|n| $n * 2} | math sum

# An empty module still has a name.
module demo {}

# Another module can be only a name.
module sample {}

# version reports this shell.
version | get version

# version alone is a complete command.
version

# Measure the version text.
version | get version | str length

# The major number can become text.
version | get major | into string

# Split the version into numeric pieces.
version | get version | split row "." | length

# Walk each column of the version record.
version | columns | each {|c| $c} | length

# Four steps from the version text to a count.
version | get version | str length | into string | str length

# PWD is the current directory.
$env.PWD | path basename

# pwd prints the working directory.
pwd

# path split breaks a directory into parts.
$env.PWD | path split | length

# Measure the last part of the working directory.
pwd | path basename | str length

# Reverse the parts of the working directory.
$env.PWD | path split | reverse | length

# Read one environment value by name.
["PWD"] | each {|n| $env | get $n} | length

# Four steps from the directory to a count.
$env.PWD | path basename | str length | into string | str length

# edit_mode names the line editing style.
$env.config.edit_mode

# show_banner says whether the intro is on.
$env.config.show_banner | into string

# Measure the edit mode name.
$env.config.edit_mode | str length | math abs

# use_ansi_coloring is true or false.
$env.config.use_ansi_coloring | into string | str length

# Count the edit mode, then count that text.
$env.config.edit_mode | str length | into string | str length

# Find one column of the config record.
$env.config | columns | where {|c| $c == "edit_mode"} | length

# Four steps from the edit mode name.
$env.config.edit_mode | str length | into string | str length | math abs

# pwd shows where you are.
pwd

# The last part of pwd is the folder name.
pwd | path basename

# ls lists the working directory.
ls | length | math abs

# path split and last name the folder.
pwd | path split | last

# Count the names ls returns.
ls | get name | length | math abs

# where can look at each listed name.
ls | where {|f| $f.name != ""} | length

# Four steps from ls to a character count.
ls | get name | length | into string | str length

# from json reads a JSON value.
'{ "n": 1 }' | from json

# from csv reads comma-separated text.
"a,b\n1,2" | from csv

# get pulls a field out of JSON.
'{ "n": 1 }' | from json | get n

# from toml reads a simple assignment.
"n = 1\n" | from toml | get n

# Read a JSON number and take abs.
'{ "n": 12 }' | from json | get n | math abs

# Walk each number in a JSON list.
'[1, 2, 3]' | from json | each {|n| $n} | math sum

# JSON to a number, then to a character count.
'{ "n": 12 }' | from json | get n | into string | str length

# str replace -r uses a regular expression.
"ab" | str replace -r "b" "c"

# parse -r captures a pattern into columns.
"abc123" | parse -r '(?P<n>\d+)'

# Read the digits a pattern captured.
"a1" | parse -r '(?P<d>\d)' | get d

# Replace a pattern, then measure the text.
"red" | str replace -r "re" "go" | str length

# Count the captures from a pattern.
"a1b2" | parse -r '(?P<d>\d)' | get d | length

# Replace a digit in each string.
["a1" "b2"] | each {|s| $s | str replace -r '\d' "n"} | length

# Capture digits and measure the text.
"abc123" | parse -r '(?P<n>\d+)' | get n | first | str length

# job spawn runs a block and returns its id.
job spawn { 1 }

# The id can be turned into text.
job spawn { 2 } | into string

# Measure the text of a job id.
job spawn { 1 } | into string | str length

# Three steps from a job id to a number.
job spawn { 1 } | into string | str length | math abs

# Four steps from a job id to a count.
job spawn { 4 } | into string | str length | into string | str length

# alias gives a short name to a command.
alias hi = print hello
hi

# An alias can stand in for math abs.
alias twice = math abs
-3 | twice

# Pipe text into an alias.
alias shout = str uppercase
"nu" | shout | str length

# An alias can be the last step of a pipe.
alias add1 = math abs
[1 2] | math sum | add1

# Measure, convert, and measure again.
alias measure = str length
"nushell" | measure | into string | str length

# An alias can follow a closure.
alias bump = math abs
[1 2] | each {|n| $n} | bump

# Four steps using an alias twice.
alias measure = str length
"tips" | measure | into string | measure | into int

# ^true runs the true program.
^true

# ^printf writes the text you give it.
^printf '%s' hi

# Pipe external output into two commands.
^printf '%s' hi | str length | math abs

# ^true succeeds, then a pipe measures text.
^true
"ok" | str length | math abs

# Three pipes from printf to a count.
^printf '%s' hi | str length | into string | str length

# Split external text and visit each character.
^printf '%s' ab | split chars | each {|c| $c} | length

# Four pipes from printf to a number.
^printf '%s' hi | str length | into string | str length | math abs

# edit_mode is emacs, vi, or helix.
$env.config.edit_mode

# keybindings list shows the current keys.
keybindings list | length

# Count the characters in the edit mode name.
$env.config.edit_mode | str length | math abs

# get name reads the keybinding column.
keybindings list | get name | length

# Count the keys, then count that text.
keybindings list | length | into string | str length

# where can keep every named keybinding.
keybindings list | where {|k| $k.name != ""} | length

# Four steps from the keybinding count.
keybindings list | length | into string | str length | math abs

# help par-each describes the parallel command.
help par-each | str length

# describe says help returned text.
help par-each | describe

# Measure the par-each help text.
help par-each | str length | math abs

# lines splits help text into rows.
help par-each | lines | length

# par-each runs a closure over a list.
[1 2 3] | par-each {|n| $n + 1} | math sum

# Sum the parallel results and take abs.
[1 2 3 4] | par-each {|n| $n} | math sum | math abs

# Four pipes through par-each to a count.
[1 2] | par-each {|n| $n + 1} | math sum | into string | str length

# metadata attaches a span to a value.
metadata 1 | describe

# metadata works on text too.
metadata "tip"

# The span record has an end field.
metadata 1 | get span | get end

# columns lists the metadata fields.
metadata "ab" | columns | length

# Count the fields inside the span.
metadata 7 | get span | columns | length

# Describe the metadata of each item.
[1 2] | each {|n| metadata $n} | describe

# Four steps from a span end to a count.
metadata 7 | get span | get end | into string | str length

# math abs drops the sign.
(-3) | math abs

# math sum adds a list.
[1 2 3] | math sum

# Sum, then take the absolute value.
[1 2 3] | math sum | math abs

# math avg and math round meet at an integer.
[1 2 3 4] | math avg | math round

# Sum, convert, and count.
[1 2 3 4] | math sum | into string | str length

# Take abs inside a closure, then sum.
[1 2 3] | each {|n| $n | math abs} | math sum

# Four math and text steps.
[1 2 3 4] | math sum | into string | str length | math abs

# path parse splits a path into fields.
"/a/b.txt" | path parse

# path basename keeps the file name.
"/a/b.txt" | path basename

# The stem is the name without the extension.
"/a/b.txt" | path parse | get stem

# path join adds one more part.
"/a/b" | path join c | path basename

# dirname, join, and basename.
"/a/b.txt" | path dirname | path join c | path basename

# Take the basename of each path.
["/a/b" "/a/c"] | each {|p| $p | path basename} | length

# Four steps from a directory to a count.
"/a/b.txt" | path dirname | path basename | str length | math abs

# date now reads the current time.
date now

# format date can print just the year.
date now | format date "%Y"

# The year text can become an integer.
date now | format date "%Y" | into int

# The month text can become an integer.
date now | format date "%m" | into int

# Year, integer, then text again.
date now | format date "%Y" | into int | into string

# Split a year-month string into parts.
date now | format date "%Y-%m" | split row "-" | length

# Four steps from the year to a count.
date now | format date "%Y" | into string | str length | math abs

# into string turns a number into text.
1 | into string

# into int turns digits into a number.
"3" | into int

# into string and into int round-trip a number.
1 | into string | into int

# into float and math round meet at an integer.
4 | into float | math round

# Text, a count, then text again.
12 | into string | str length | into string

# Convert each number inside a closure.
[1 2] | each {|n| $n | into string} | length

# Four conversions from a number to a count.
12 | into string | str length | into string | str length

# random int draws from a range.
random int 1..3

# random bool is true or false.
random bool | into string

# A random integer can be shown as text.
random int 1..5 | math abs | into string

# random uuid is text you can measure.
random uuid | str length | math abs

# Three steps from a random integer.
random int 1..9 | into string | str length | math abs

# Draw a bool for each list item.
[1 2 3] | each {|n| random bool} | length

# Four steps from a random integer to a count.
random int 1..9 | into string | str length | into string | str length

# bits and keeps the bits set in both numbers.
2 | bits and 3

# bits shl shifts bits to the left.
1 | bits shl 3

# or, then and, combines two bit checks.
2 | bits or 1 | bits and 3

# Shift left, then take abs.
1 | bits shl 2 | math abs

# Shift left, shift right, then abs.
1 | bits shl 3 | bits shr 1 | math abs

# Shift each number inside a closure.
[1 2 3] | each {|n| $n | bits shl 1} | math sum

# Four bit and text steps.
1 | bits shl 4 | bits shr 1 | into string | str length

# bytes length counts binary bytes.
0x[01 02] | bytes length

# encode utf8 turns text into bytes.
"ab" | encode utf8

# Count the bytes in a short string.
"hi" | encode utf8 | bytes length

# bytes reverse flips the byte order.
0x[01 02 03] | bytes reverse | bytes length

# A byte count can become text.
"hi" | encode utf8 | bytes length | into string

# Encode each string inside a closure.
["a" "b"] | each {|s| $s | encode utf8} | length

# Four steps from text to a character count.
"hi" | encode utf8 | bytes length | into string | str length

# sys host includes the hostname.
sys host | get hostname

# sys cpu returns one row per cpu.
sys cpu | length

# Measure the hostname.
sys host | get hostname | str length

# The cpu row count is a number.
sys cpu | length | math abs

# Hostname length, then abs.
sys host | get hostname | str length | math abs

# each can visit every cpu row.
sys cpu | each {|c| $c} | length

# Four steps from the hostname to a count.
sys host | get hostname | str length | into string | str length

# history lists commands from this shell.
history | length

# history session is the current session id.
history session | into string

# The history length is a number.
history | length | math abs

# Measure the session id text.
history session | into string | str length

# Count the history, then count that text.
history | length | into string | str length

# Filter the history column names.
history | columns | where {|c| $c != ""} | length

# Four steps from the history length.
history | length | into string | str length | math abs

# hash md5 fingerprints text.
"hi" | hash md5

# hash sha256 is a longer fingerprint.
"hi" | hash sha256

# An md5 fingerprint has a fixed length.
"hi" | hash md5 | str length

# A sha256 fingerprint has a fixed length.
"tip" | hash sha256 | str length

# Measure a fingerprint and take abs.
"hi" | hash md5 | str length | math abs

# Hash each string inside a closure.
["a" "b"] | each {|s| $s | hash md5} | length

# Four steps from text to a character count.
"hi" | hash md5 | str length | into string | str length

# seq builds a range of numbers.
seq 1 3 | math sum

# length counts the numbers seq made.
seq 1 4 | length

# Sum a sequence, then take abs.
seq 1 4 | math sum | math abs

# seq char walks letters.
seq char a c | length | math abs

# Sum a sequence and count the text.
seq 1 5 | math sum | into string | str length

# Add one to each generated number.
seq 1 3 | each {|n| $n + 1} | math sum

# Four steps from a sequence to a count.
seq 1 4 | math sum | into string | str length | math abs

# url parse splits a URL into fields.
"https://example.com/a" | url parse

# A different URL parses the same way.
"https://example.com/b" | url parse

# get host reads the host field.
"https://example.com/a" | url parse | get host

# url join rebuilds a URL from its fields.
"https://example.com/a" | url parse | url join

# Measure the host name.
"https://example.com/docs" | url parse | get host | str length

# Measure the path field.
"https://example.com/a?b=1" | url parse | get path | str length

# Four steps from a URL to a number.
"https://e.com/docs" | url parse | get host | str length | math abs

# A tensor is a native array of numbers.
use torch
torch tensor [1 2 3] | torch value

# Read the shape, then count its axes.
use torch
torch tensor [1 2 3] | torch shape | length

# Sum the values and describe the result.
use torch
torch tensor [1 2 3] | torch sum | torch value | describe

# Sum, show, and measure the printed form.
use torch
torch tensor [1 2 3] | torch sum | torch value | describe | str length

# ones builds a tensor filled with one.
use torch
torch ones [2]

# Sum a vector of ones and read it.
use torch
torch ones [2] | torch sum | torch value

# An identity matrix summed down to a scalar.
use torch
torch eye 2 | torch sum | torch abs | torch value

# Build, negate, sum, and read a vector.
use torch
torch ones [2] | torch neg | torch abs | torch sum | torch value

# abs flips negative numbers to positive.
use torch
torch tensor [-1 2] | torch abs

# Multiply a tensor by itself.
use torch
let x = torch tensor [2 3]
$x | torch mul $x | torch value

# Square a tensor, then take abs.
use torch
let x = torch tensor [-2 3]
$x | torch mul $x | torch abs | torch value

# Square, clean, sum, and read.
use torch
let x = torch tensor [1 2 3]
$x | torch mul $x | torch abs | torch sum | torch value

# sum adds every element.
use torch
torch tensor [1 2 3] | torch sum

# mean of a small vector.
use torch
torch tensor [1.0 3.0] | torch mean | torch value

# Sum of absolute values.
use torch
torch tensor [-1 2] | torch abs | torch sum | torch value

# Absolute value, sum, abs, and value.
use torch
torch tensor [1 2 3] | torch abs | torch sum | torch abs | torch value

# reshape changes the axes, not the values.
use torch
torch tensor [1 2 3 4] | torch reshape [2 2]

# Count axes after a reshape.
use torch
torch tensor [1 2 3 4] | torch reshape [2 2] | torch shape

# Transpose, flatten, and count axes.
use torch
torch eye 2 | torch t | torch flatten | torch shape

# Transpose, flatten, sum, and read.
use torch
torch eye 2 | torch t | torch flatten | torch sum | torch value

# trace adds the diagonal of a matrix.
use torch
torch eye 2 | torch trace

# Multiply a matrix by itself.
use torch
let a = torch eye 2
$a | torch mm $a | torch value

# Trace, abs, and value.
use torch
torch eye 2 | torch trace | torch abs | torch value

# Transpose, trace, abs, and value.
use torch
torch eye 2 | torch t | torch trace | torch abs | torch value

# mse_loss compares a guess with a target.
use torch
let pred = torch tensor [1.0 0.0]
let target = torch tensor [1.0 0.0]
torch mse_loss $pred $target

# Read the mean squared error as a value.
use torch
let p = torch tensor [1.0 0.0]
let t = torch tensor [1.0 0.0]
torch mse_loss $p $t | torch abs | torch value

# Absolute error, summed and read.
use torch
let p = torch tensor [1.0 0.0]
let t = torch tensor [0.0 1.0]
torch l1_loss $p $t | torch abs | torch sum | torch value

# Four steps from a loss to a value.
use torch
let p = torch tensor [1.0]
let t = torch tensor [0.0]
torch l1_loss $p $t | torch abs | torch sum | torch abs | torch value

# eq compares a tensor with itself.
use torch
let a = torch tensor [1 2]
$a | torch eq $a

# allclose reports whether two tensors agree.
use torch
let a = torch tensor [1.0]
$a | torch allclose $a | into string

# Sum an equality mask and read it.
use torch
let a = torch tensor [1 2]
$a | torch eq $a | torch sum | torch value

# Equality, sum, abs, and value.
use torch
let a = torch tensor [1 2]
$a | torch eq $a | torch sum | torch abs | torch value

# manual_seed makes the next random draw repeatable.
use torch
torch manual_seed 1
torch ones [1]

# Seed, then sum a vector of ones.
use torch
torch manual_seed 1
torch ones [2] | torch sum | torch value

# Seed, then sum the absolute values.
use torch
torch manual_seed 2
torch ones [2] | torch abs | torch sum | torch value

# Seed, negate, abs, sum, and read.
use torch
torch manual_seed 3
torch ones [2] | torch neg | torch abs | torch sum | torch value

# requires-grad marks a tensor for differentiation.
use torch
let x = torch tensor [2.0] --requires-grad
$x | torch sum

# Sum a tracked vector and read the scalar.
use torch
let x = torch tensor [2.0] --requires-grad
$x | torch sum | torch value

# Square, sum, and backpropagate.
use torch
let x = torch tensor [2.0] --requires-grad
$x | torch mul $x | torch sum | torch backward

# Backpropagate, then read the gradient.
use torch
let x = torch tensor [2.0] --requires-grad
$x | torch mul $x | torch sum | torch backward
$x | torch grad | torch value

# A linear layer maps features to outputs.
use torch
torch nn linear 2 1

# Forward a row through a new linear layer.
use torch
let model = torch nn linear 2 1
torch tensor [1.0 0.0] | torch forward $model | torch value

# Build a tiny stack and describe it.
use torch
let model = torch nn sequential (torch nn linear 2 1) (torch nn relu)
torch nn info $model | describe | str length | math abs

# Call one forward pass from a command you can reuse.
use torch
def score [] {
  let model = torch nn linear 2 1
  torch tensor [1.0 0.0] | torch forward $model | torch value
}
score
